author: zero1develop
content:
ZERO1 Groth16 Trusted Setup Ceremony — Launch Announcement
Hey everyone! 👋
We are excited to announce that the ZERO1 Phase 2 Trusted Setup Ceremony is officially LIVE! 🎉
About ZERO1
At ZERO1, we believe privacy shouldn't come at the price of trust. We are building a decentralized, trustless privacy-preserving yield protocol—no backdoors, no intermediaries, just open-source, verifiable Groth16 ZK circuits.
Why Your Contribution Matters
The security of our Groth16 circuits relies on a 1-of-N trust assumption: as long as just one participant honestly generates randomness and discards their toxic waste, the final parameters are cryptographically secure for everyone.
How to Participate
1. Visit the Ceremony Portal: https://ceremony.zero1develop.com/
2. Sign in: Connect with your GitHub or X (Twitter) account.
3. Contribute Entropy: Follow the on-screen instructions on your computer to add your randomness to the circuit parameters.
Links
• Ceremony Page: https://ceremony.zero1develop.com/
• Project Home & Roadmap: https://zero1develop.com/
Every single contribution strengthens the cryptographic foundation of public privacy infrastructure. Thank you for helping us build a trustless future—feel free to drop your contribution hash in the thread below once you're done! 🛡️✨

author: sky.cactus
content: Why is signin necessary to participate in a trusted setup ceremony for an allegedly private protocol?  Seems like starting off on the wrong foot.

author: zero1develop
content: Participants are required to attend the ceremony using an X or GitHub account. The main benefits are to increase the cost of witch attacks, improve queue management, and provide publicly verifiable participation identities.

author: zero1develop
content: Welcome everyone to our ceremony. Our circuit adds a bit of entropy.

author: sky.cactus
content: Why not use one of the ZK proof-of-unique-human systems as an option, or let people burn/transfer a bit of money instead if they want to participate anonymously?
